GTA 6 Pre Order Data Shows Xbox Now at 23% of the 4.38 Million Total

By Ray Ampoloquio · Aug 19, 2026
Updated by Matt Gibbs · Aug 19, 2026

Xbox Series X|S preorders for Grand Theft Auto VI have topped 1 million, per Sensor Tower estimates, about 23% of the tracked 4.38 million total.

Zoom image: Grand Theft Auto VI pre-orders passed 4.38 million, with Xbox crossing 1 million, per Sensor Tower.
Grand Theft Auto VI pre-orders keep ticking up. According to Sensor Tower , the analytics firm running a public sales tracker for the game, the next Grand Theft Auto added roughly 80,000 pre-orders over the past week, nudging the total to about 4.38 million with roughly a million of that being for the Xbox Series X|S.

Of course, these are merely estimates. While Sensor Tower is a legitimate analytics company, they don't have access to the actual sales sheet. The only people who know the real numbers are at Rockstar Games , Take-Two Interactive and likely Sony and Microsoft, and they are not telling a soul, with Take-Two only calling pre-order interest "unprecedented ."

With that said, Xbox crossing a million pre-orders is a win. Previously, it was reported that PS5 orders were outselling Xbox sales 6-to-1 . The latest figures paint a much closer fight, with Xbox pre-orders sitting at about 23% of the total. Naturally, Rockstar's exclusive marketing partnership with Sony steered attention toward PlayStation from the very start, so the Xbox pre-orders that have piled up regardless suggest a dedicated base uninterested in switching platforms.

These are third-party estimates from Sensor Tower's model, not official numbers from Rockstar or the platform holders.

Pre-orders opened back in late June, so this is the quiet middle stretch, the lull after the diehards have already committed and before the launch rush starts. Sensor Tower's own analysts have said the vast majority of pre-orders arrive in the final week or two before a game ships, so a steady trickle of 80,000 a week right now is the calm before the actual number shows up.

Besides, between the leaks and the upcoming Netflix premiere, GTA 6 pre-orders over the next two weeks will dwarf this figure.

The 4.38 million works out to an estimated $429 million already committed, months before launch , which is why the game could essentially pay for itself before anyone plays it . It is also inflated by the fact that nearly nine in ten of those buyers are choosing the $100 Ultimate Edition over the $80 standard, a split that has analysts genuinely baffled.

None of this is a shock and none of it is the finish line. The number that actually matters is the one Sensor Tower cannot estimate yet, the launch-week total, and we will not see the real surge until the countdown to November 19 gets a lot shorter.

For now, GTA 6 is doing exactly what everyone expected , quietly, one modest weekly bump at a time.

GTA 6 Leaker Cyberleek Picked a Fight It Cannot Win Against Take Two

By Ray Ampoloquio · Aug 18, 2026
Updated by Matt Gibbs · Aug 19, 2026

Rockstar and Take Two have stayed silent on Cyberleek's manifesto, instead issuing DMCA takedowns to erase the leaked GTA VI footage and map.

Zoom image: History says leaks barely dent Take-Two, one even added a billion, and the leaker is the one at risk the most.
After the footage and map dump wrapped in a crypto scam and the group behind it issuing a manifesto of demands , the only real question left following the latest Grand Theft Auto VI leak is what happens now.

While we don't know what Rockstar Games and Take-Two Interactive will do, we do have a hunch that both will follow the same playback it did before. If their history with such incidents tells us anything, this entire fiasco will end as a nuisance rather than a complete disaster.

So far, Take-Two has carpet bombed the internet with copyright takedowns, hitting the original posts, the reuploads, and the mirrors on X and everywhere else, fast enough that the footage is already getting hard to find. What it has not done, and almost certainly will not do, is address it, the three commandments, or the demand for an apology and "restitution."

Their silence is a choice . It is staying quiet because responding to the manifesto, even to reject it, would hand those demands attention and a smidge of legitimacy. The moment a company argues with a hacktivist wishlist, it's entertaining the idea of the wishlist and this isn't the best time nor platform to do that. So, the best course of action is to act like it doesn't exist, nuke the copyrighted material, and starve the news cycle because the next Grand Theft Auto event is just right around the corner .

You see, leaks just don't hurt the company the way you'd expect them. Most of the time, these become free marketing for GTA , absorbed into the game's short and intense marketing cycle so far .

How the last three big Take-Two leaks actually played out
Leak

What got out

Market reaction

How it ended

September 2022 (Lapsus$)

Early GTA 6 development footage

Shares dipped, then mostly recovered within a day

The hacker was caught and convicted; the game stayed on track

April 2026 (ShinyHunters)

GTA Online and Red Dead Online revenue data

Market value rose around $1 billion

Read as proof of how profitable the online mode is

August 2026 (Cyberleek)

Older-build gameplay, a map, a manifesto, a memecoin

No clear reaction so far

DMCA takedowns underway, no comment on the demands

Two of these barely moved the stock, and one actually made Take-Two richer. This is not a company that leaks tend to hurt.

The big 2022 development-footage leak , the one everyone remembers, knocked the stock down a couple of percent and it clawed back most of it within a day, once Rockstar confirmed the game was fine.

Then in April 2026, a completely different crew leaked internal Grand Theft Auto Online revenue numbers and instead of tanking, Take-Two's market value climbed by roughly a billion dollars , because the breach accidentally advertised how obscenely profitable the online mode is , showing investors a spreadsheet that they liked and wanted to see more of going forward.

The Cyberleek material, older-build and a map before the potential official reveal, does not even reach the level of either of those.

The leaker picked a fight with a company that has functionally unlimited legal money and a proven willingness to spend it. The 2022 hacker who leaked the original footage, part of the Lapsus$ group, was tracked down, arrested, and convicted . Even Rockstar developers are "terrified" of the company's lawyers and Cyberleek built a website, published a manifesto, named a memecoin after itself, and keeps threatening more.

Everything it does is leaving a breadcrumb for authorities to follow. The louder it becomes on the internet, the easier it gets to find, and the harder it becomes to pretend this was some curious kid poking around a server.

So what actually changes? Almost nothing. The demands will not budge video game industry's digital-only plans an inch , the stock will not crater, development will not slip, and the grievances underneath all of it, the disc-free launch , the locked content , the games that die when servers go dark, stay exactly as real and exactly as unaddressed as they were last week.

Right now, the only timeline that matters is the official one and it hasn't moved at all. By the time the latest GTA 6 footage premieres on Netflix on August 27 and comes out in November , people will remember Cyberleek less for its commandments than for how fast the company it tried to strong-arm made the whole thing vanish.

GTA 6 Leaker Cyberleek Issues Three Demands To Take Two

By Ray Ampoloquio · Aug 18, 2026
Updated by Matt Gibbs · Aug 19, 2026

Cyberleek stole GTA 6 footage and is funding its "commandments" with a memecoin. Don't expect Take Two to negotiate, apologize, or pay restitution.

Zoom image: The Cyberleek group behind the GTA 6 leak issued three demands to Rockstar and Take-Two.
Cyberleek , the account that dumped stolen GTA 6 gameplay and a map image on August 18 while quietly running a memecoin on the side, has followed it up with three "commandments" for Rockstar Games , Take-Two Interactive , and every other big publisher, saying it is the bare minimum it will accept before it stops going after them.

The crazy part here is that if you look beyond the ones responsible for saying it, most Grand Theft Auto fans would agree with what they have to say and what they are fighting for.

Cyberleek argues nobody should pay for a game through a storefront before it is out and before reviews exist, and that if publishers want your money early, they can go back to pressing discs like the old days.

They're also arguing against fake single-player DLC , meaning publishers should stop charging you for content already sitting inside the game files you bought.

Finally, they're pushing for preservation. That single-player games should ship with an offline fallback so they still work if the servers get switched off, which is the same fight preservationists have been having over dead games like The Crew .

The grievances are real. GTA 6 is launching with no physical disc at all , publishers really do lock content behind paywalls that some players suspect was on the disc the whole time , games really do get killed off with the money kept and the servers pulled, the same concern that has Grand Theft Auto Online players nervous about their own community servers .

Cyberleek's three commandments, translated
The demand

What it actually means

The reality

No digital preorders

Stop letting people pay before launch and before reviews exist; press physical discs instead

Popular idea, zero chance a publisher adopts it under threat

No fake single-player DLC

Stop charging for content already sitting in the game files you bought

A real grievance, though "fake" is doing a lot of undefined work

Preserve single-player games

Ship a final offline patch so games still run if the servers die

The most defensible one, and closest to a real movement

Three demands most players would happily sign, attached to a hack and a memecoin nobody asked for.

The message, indeed, is popular. The problem? It's the messenger. What they're doing is still utterly wrong.

This is a group that stole footage, is threatening to keep hacking anyone who breaks its rules, insists a public apology is not enough because "restitution is mandatory," and is bankrolling the whole crusade with a cryptocurrency called $CYBERLEEK. The people demanding Take-Two stop treating fans like a revenue stream are, at the very same time, trying to use those same fans for a quick cash grab.

Will it work? Probably not. Take-Two is a public company. It doesn't negotiate with hackers and people responsible for data breaching because doing so opens a whole can of worms, inviting others to try and do the same. Don't expect an apology, a concrete commitment, or restitution. What will happen here are lawyers working overtime, takedown notices flying everywhere, and silence, which is already exactly what is happening. Extortion is a terrible delivery system for a wishlist, however agreeable the wishlist is.

By bolting genuinely reasonable demands onto theft, threats, and a crypto grift, Cyberleek is not advancing any of this. It is poisoning it. Ending pay-before-you-see-it preorders, real preservation and honest DLC are serious conversations that the industry needs to have. Handing them to a hacker with a memecoin lets publishers get away clean by giving them a villain to point to and changing the subject.

None of this changes anything. There's a reason why the GTA 6 boycott is a non-event . The people with real leverage here are not hackers issuing commandments, but the millions who have already paid full price. Until that changes, nothing will. Rockstar's Extended Look still premieres on Netflix on August 27 , GTA 6 still launches on November 19 , and these three commandments will become a footnote by the time either arrives.

The demands deserve a better champion than the one currently holding them hostage.

Take-Two Issues DMCA Takedown Notices Over GTA 6 Gameplay Leaks

Take-Two Interactive has been issuing DMCA takedown notices on yesterday’s leaked GTA 6 gameplay videos, suggesting that at the very least, they are real.

The GTA 6 gameplay leaks surfaced yesterday, with the alleged leaker stating that he leaked the footage primarily because GTA 6 will be a digital-only title.

GTA 6 Gameplay Leaks Are Real

Take-Two Interactive has been spending the last 12 or so, at the time of writing, aggressively taking down the GTA 6 gameplay videos that have leaked online, suggesting that the leaks are real.

However, as those who have seen the gameplay may have realized, the game doesn’t meet the standard you would expect just mere months away from release.

That’s because, according to the video’s metadata , the GTA gameplay videos are from around 2023. So worry not, these are old gameplay videos.

RELATED: Will GTA 6 Be Delayed Again?

That being said, we are only a week away from finally seeing actual recent gameplay of GTA 6 in the Netflix special, which airs on August 27, 2026.

Insider Gaming also understands that previews of GTA 6 are underway, which will likely coincide with the event. Notice how some outlets and content creators didn’t cover the recent leaks? It’s probably because they don’t want to rub people the wrong way who’ve invited them to get hands-on with Grand Theft Auto 6.

As for what’s next with GTA 6 leaks and the leaker, the leaker claims that he will leak more from other developers and publishers, but it’s unclear whether the leaks are just tied to one event, and whether or not the leaker is bluffing to try and capitalize on the recent events.

Regardless, he will undoubtedly be targeted now by Take-Two Interactive, and likely have to face the consequences.

New GTA 6 Leak Pairs Likely Genuine Gameplay With Risky Crypto Links

By Ray Ampoloquio · Aug 18, 2026
Updated by Matt Gibbs · Aug 18, 2026

The leaked GTA 6 gameplay clips and map look genuine, but the leaker pushes crypto QR codes & links, so avoid those & wait for Rockstar's own reveal.

Nine days before Rockstar Games was planning to show us Grand Theft Auto VI on its own terms, someone else did it first. A batch of leaked gameplay footage and a supposed full map of Leonida hit social media on Tuesday, August 18, and this time, unlike the last few scares , a lot of it, if not all of it, looks very likely to be real.

What's included in the latest Grand Theft Auto leak are short gameplay clips. In one, Jason is hanging around his oceanside house from the second trailer , and in another, he sideswipes a delivery truck, brawls with the furious driver, picks up a wrench, and pulls a two-star wanted level. On top of the clips, there is a high-resolution image going around that shows off the entirety of Leonida , naming counties and spots we haven't seen before.

Normally, we'd brush off leaks these this, but Take-Two Interactive didn't, which is telling.

Not more than an hour after the clips made their way to various social media platforms, Take-Two's legal team did their jobs and started hitting posts with copyright takedowns. As of this writing, Take-Two is trying to contain the entire situation and they are yet to release a statement. However, we fear that the cat is already out of the bag.

GTA 6 Leaked Contents
What surfaced

The read

The gameplay clips (basketball, road rage)

Very likely genuine. Novel mechanics, trailer-matching visuals, RDR2-style animation, and multiple outlets treating it as real. Reportedly from an older build

A "full map" of Leonida

Shakier. It closely matches long-running fan maps, so it could be real or a cleaned-up repackage of community work

The DMCA takedowns

Not proof on their own. Take-Two strikes convincing fakes too. The un-fakeable detail is what sells it, not the strike

How it is being spread

A red flag. The leaker is pushing crypto sites and QR codes, so treat the source as a likely scam

The footage looks real, the map may be genuine, and the source is a potential malware attack.

The gameplay clips look genuine in a way that the 2022 leaks were . The amount of detail is ridiculous. AI can't replicate this . There's a ton of specific, novel, internally consistent stuff that would take an impossible amount of work to fake convincingly, and it lines up with the trailers and the pre-order screenshots we've gotten so far.

We won't go into much detail about what the leaks contained, but we will tell you that GTA 6 is definitely looking like it will meet all expectations , and then some.

Reports are also suggesting that the footage is from an older build, maybe as far back as 2023, which says a lot about how much better Vice City and the rest of GTA 6 will look, feel, and play come November .

Now, as for where the leaks are coming from, the account pushing all of this, posting as Cyberleek, is wrapping the footage in cryptocurrency promos, QR codes, and links to a crypto site, asking people to pay up for more. Even if every frame of the leak is real, the delivery is a scam waiting to happen. Do not fall for it.

When you show almost nothing for years, every a blurry, out-of-context, scam-adjacent clip feels like a revelation and the takedowns become synonymous with gospel. It's easy to argue Rockstar's silence created the same vacuum that let a fake Netflix listing spread two weeks ago , except this time the leak looks real. Even then, Take-Two strikes convincing fakes just as fast as it strikes actual leaks , so it might not even be true.

With that said, none of this needed to leak. We're days away from the next official GTA 6 showcase, which premieres on Netflix on August 27 , in high quality, in context, with sound, and without a crypto scam bolted to it, ahead of the game's launch .

So if you ever feel tempted, try to fight it . You already waited this long. You can wait a few more days and skip the QR code while you are at it.

GTA 4 Almost Gave Every NPC a Home and a Job Before Rockstar Scrapped It

By Ray Ampoloquio · Aug 18, 2026
Updated by Matt Gibbs · Aug 18, 2026

Grand Theft Auto VI was meant to give NPCs homes and jobs in a living, breathing version of Liberty City, but Rockstar scrapped it as too messy.

Obbe Vermeij , the former Rockstar North technical director who worked on everything from Grand Theft Auto III through Grand Theft Auto IV , told Edge magazine that Grand Theft Auto IV was meant to have a genuinely living population, an idea that's about to come to life in Grand Theft Auto V thanks to the RP scene over a decade later.

According to the longtime Rockstar Games developer, producer Leslie Benzies wanted every NPC in Liberty City to have its own life. The idea was a city that kept running, full of people with somewhere to go and stuff to do. Unfortunately, the brilliant folks over at Rockstar were limited by the technology of their time.

Vermeij says the team chipped away at it for a while before giving up, because the whole thing turned into a mess, adding that he didn't even think it mattered. In his view, players are perfectly comfortable with pedestrians that are a bit hollow and artificial, as long as the city around them feels alive, which makes sense considering he once told us that Rockstar's cities have always run on illusion rather than simulation , and that the thing which actually shatters the spell is not a shallow NPC but an NPC that walks headfirst into a wall.

Vermeij was wrong though. Aside from the aforementioned AI-powered RP server, Rockstar's own Red Dead Redemption 2 delivered a real chunk of this once-dropped feature, NPCs with routines and even a kind of memory, townsfolk who would greet you differently the second time around depending on how the first meeting went.

The living-NPC dream across three Rockstar games
Game

The living-NPC idea

Grand Theft Auto IV ( 2008 )

Benzies wanted NPCs with homes, schedules, and daily commutes. Scrapped after too many bugs

Red Dead Redemption 2 ( 2018 )

NPCs got real routines and behavioral memory, greeting you differently on a second visit

Grand Theft Auto VI ( 2026 )

Reportedly the most reactive NPC systems Rockstar has attempted, still unproven until launch

The idea Vermeij shrugged off in 2008 kept resurfacing, better funded each time.

The timing of all this is genuinely funny, because the feature Vermeij waved away as not worth the trouble is now, seventeen years later, basically the headline promise of Grand Theft Auto VI and its fresh, new depiction of Leonida and our return to Vice City. Every leak and expectation points to the most reactive, most simulated city Rockstar has ever attempted . The dream got deferred, and it kept coming back with a bigger budget behind it .

Yet, Vermeij wasn't entirely wrong. Even Red Dead Redemption 2 , even whatever GTA 6 manages, is still mostly a magic trick. Those NPCs do not really have lives. They have convincing routines that exist inside the little bubble around you and switch off the moment you leave it. Rockstar got extraordinarily good at the illusion. It never actually built the simulation, because the illusion is the part that matters.

So if you are picturing a GTA 6 where every person on the street genuinely has a home to drive back to, they almost certainly won't. Vice City and Los Santos will feel alive. The NPCs in it just won't have actual lives, and we'll find how how convincing the latest version of Rockstar's decades-long trick is on November 19 .

GTA Vice City Now Runs Natively on GameCube Hardware Thanks to Fan Port

By Ray Ampoloquio · Aug 18, 2026
Updated by Matt Gibbs · Aug 18, 2026

A modder got GTA: Vice City running natively on real GameCube hardware, targeting 640x480 with full PC textures & 60fps capped, around 90fps uncapped.

More than two decades after the Nintendo GameCube came and went without a single Grand Theft Auto game, someone is finally giving it a GTA title, and it's running much better on what is technically Nintendo's last home console.

The Brazilian developer posting as Ebellumat shared about two and a half minutes of footage this month showing Grand Theft Auto: Vice City running natively on real GameCube hardware, cruising around Vice City at night, driving, brawling, radar and wanted stars and all.

For those who have already forgotten, GTA: Vice City was a PlayStation 2 game first, only later reaching Xbox and PC. The GameCube, which launched around the same time, never got Vice City , Grand Theft Auto III before it, or any mainline GTA at all. This is why this port is such a big deal, especially when you consider that Nintendo consoles has never gotten a mainline GTA title outside of the Nintendo Switch getting the Grand Theft Auto: The Trilogy - The Definitive Edition , or being modded to run Grand Theft Auto V .

To make it possible the project uses reVC, an open, reverse-engineered recreation of GTA: Vice City often used by modders to get the game running on other platforms. For help, EBellumat leaned on the code from the GTA 3 port for the Sega Dreamcast built by Falco Girgis and his team. Girgis, rather than getting territorial about someone borrowing his work, cheered the whole thing on, saying he never doubted the GameCube could handle GTA: Vice City and that it is "handling it better than either DC or PS2 can."

What the GameCube Vice City port Is Targeting
Feature

Target

Resolution

640 by 480

Frame rate

60 fps, capped (it was hitting around 90 uncapped in testing)

Textures

Full PC-quality textures

Effects

All of them switched on

Audio

32 kHz stereo

Widescreen

Everything from 4:3 up to 21:9, thanks to reVC

Here's what the developer wants to achieve for their GTA: Vice City port on the Nintendo GameCube.

The GameCube not getting any Grand Theft Auto in the 2000s was never really a power problem and this port proves that. Nintendo's console had a genuinely strong general-purpose processor, better suited to the physics, streaming, and animation that GTA leans on than the PlayStation 2's more awkward chip.

What actually kept these games off the GameCube was its tiny mini-discs that topped out around 1.5 gigabytes, well short of the full DVDs the PS2 and Xbox used. Its audience also skewed younger and more family-minded, a hard sell for a game built around mowing down pedestrians in a neon crime playground. Finally, Nintendo's whole image at the time pointed in the opposite direction. So the machine got written off as the wrong home for GTA and years later a hobbyist is quietly showing that the engineering was never the thing in the way.

None of this is official. reVC-style projects live in the same legal gray zone all of these ports do and Take-Two Interactive has gone after the reverse-engineered GTA code before. EBellumat is threading the same needle everyone threads. He plans to open the source shortly, under a quirky, very-2026 license that is basically MIT with an attendance list for any AI models that train on it.

It all sits alongside the same stubborn preservation streak that recently got Vice City Stories running natively on PC and handed the Dreamcast a playable Vice City of its own . The familiar pattern never changes. Rockstar Games leaves an old game stranded, the community refuses to let it stay there, and somebody spends their nights proving a twenty-year-old console could have run it all along.

The GameCube waited a very long time for GTA . Turns out it was ready the whole time.

By Ray Ampoloquio · Aug 18, 2026
Updated by Matt Gibbs · Aug 18, 2026

Running well on Xbox Series S isn't guaranteed for GTA 6. Analysts expect low resolution and cut ray tracing just to hold 30fps on that console.

"If Grand Theft Auto VI can run on the Xbox Series S, why can't your game hit 60 frames per second on it?" is the question and argument many fans are using against developers these days, and Thomas Mahler, the founder of Moon Studios, has finally had enough.

Mahler, whose studio made the Ori games and No Rest for the Wicked , fired off a blunt reply. Here's an excerpt of what he said on X :

I just love comments like: "How dare your game isn't running at 60fps on Xbox Series S yet when GTA VI will run on it?!?!" 1) We don't know yet how well that thing will run. 2) Well, gee, I don't know, MAYBE it's because Rockstar literally just spent over a billion dollars and had THOUSANDS of people working on it for over a decade now?

He was not much kinder about the Series S itself, describing it as a cheap machine with less usable memory than a Valve Steam Deck and writing off the loudest demands as fanboyism from people who do not understand the tech. He isn't lying. The Xbox Series S is Microsoft's cheaper current-generation console, the little white one that launched at $299 that's half the console its big brother, the Xbox Series X, is, figuratively and literally.

Despite coming from the same console generation, the Xbox Series S and Xbox Series X are very different machines.

The Series S has roughly a third of the Series X's graphics muscle and, once the system takes its cut, only about eight gigabytes of memory for the actual game. Developers have wrestled with this technical ceiling for years, especially after Microsoft required nearly every Xbox game ship on both machines.

This means the weakest box in the room sets the limit for everyone and Mahler is right that pinning that responsibility on a small studio while pointing at a project with the kind of unlimited budget GTA 6 has at its disposal is not a fair fight.

With that said, analysts at Digital Foundry are expecting the Series S version to drop as low as 720p with ray tracing gutted just to hold a stable 30, so very few with technical know-how are are optimistic that GTA 6 will run well on the pint-sized console. It's not just on the Series S, either: multiple experts, and a former Rockstar animator, think GTA 6 will be locked to 30 frames per second on every current-gen console , the PlayStation 5 and Series X included, because Rockstar obsesses over visual detail more than frame rates .

This still doesn't change the fact that the Series S has become the anchor dragging on this console generation, the reason ambitious games keep getting clipped or delayed, and players are not wrong to express their annoyance. They're just better off pointing it at the right target. Moon Studios didn't build the Series S. Rockstar didn't, either.

Microsoft did, and it's the one requiring developers to make sure every game they release this console generation also runs well on the Series S. If there's anyone who deserves all the fingers pointed to it, it's Microsoft. Ultimately, this is what's become of GTA 6 : it's a a performance yardstick for other games even though it's not even released yet. It's come to a point that it's winning performance arguments before fans can preload it .

Fingers crossed, we'll get a slightly better sense of how it looks in motion when the Extended Look hits Netflix on August 27 with at least a smidge of gameplay footage .

An Army Unit Is Reportedly Offering Days Off to Play GTA 6

By Ray Ampoloquio · Aug 18, 2026
Updated by Matt Gibbs · Aug 18, 2026

A viral memo claims a Fort Stewart Army battalion offers reenlisting soldiers four days off starting the day after Grand Theft Auto 6 launches.

A memo making the rounds online claims that a U.S. Army battalion is offering its soldiers four days off to play Grand Theft Auto 6 as a reward for re-enlisting. The document, dated July 28, is addressed to everyone in the 9th Brigade Engineer Battalion, a real unit stationed at Fort Stewart, Georgia, laying out a "Special Reenlistment Incentive" tied directly to the next Grand Theft Auto .

It states that any active-duty enlisted soldier in the battalion who signs a new contract between August 1 and November 14 gets a special four-day pass running November 20 through 23, so the leave kicks in the very next morning GTA 6 comes out .

According to the letter, the goal is to boost retention and morale, which is a a bureaucratic way of saying the Army would like people to re-up and it noticed that a lot of them are huge fans of Rockstar Games ' best-selling franchise.

The catch? It isn't exactly a vacation. It is a short stretch of authorised time off, you need your company commander to sign off, you cannot bolt it onto other leave to stretch it into a real trip, and you are out entirely if you have administrative flags or you are failing physical fitness or body composition standards, which you might if you end up letting yourself go while going Kai Cenat on GTA 6 .

The people, the unit, and the dates are all real. The memo itself isn't officially verified.

The image went viral because of the military meme page, "USA Army WTF!? Moments," and spread everywhere from there . Many outlets have reached out and couldn't confirm its authenticity. However, a suspicious number of details hold up, from the commander's name to the communication numbers in the header to formatting that enlisted soldiers say matches the real thing.

Lieutenant Colonel Ryan D. Hodgson, whose signature sits at the bottom, really did take command of the battalion back in July, and plenty of veterans online basically shrugged it off, since unit commanders have a reputation for offering creative time-off bribes to beef up re-enlistment numbers. Which brings us to the part that actually matters, real or not, and that's the fact that this is instantly believable.

Nobody blinked at the idea of the United States Army building a retention incentive around a video game launch because GTA is that game. We have already watched a 78-year-old grandmother buy an Xbox just to be there for it , companies float launch-day time off or fielding a skeletal workforce , and the entire video game industry rearranging their entire holiday season around it .

Even the official White House social media account used GTA in a recent video . When viewed from that perspective, a game reaching the point where the military might use it to keep soldiers in uniform is just the next logical, faintly absurd rung on that ladder.

5 Things the GTA 6 Extended Look on Netflix Probably Won't Show

By Ray Ampoloquio · Aug 18, 2026
Updated by Matt Gibbs · Aug 18, 2026

The Netflix Extended Look on August 27 will spotlight Jason & Lucia, but expect no full map, no GTA Online details, no PC news, and no real gameplay.

Every countdown to a big Grand Theft Auto VI moment comes with the same promise, and the Extended Look hitting Netflix on August 27 is no different. It's also worth telling yourself to calm down first and manage expectations, but probably not for the reasons you think you should. Rockstar Games has never really worked the way the rest of the industry has, which is a good thing.

This is a studio that guards its biggest cards until launch day and drips the rest out on a careful schedule. Even Take-Two Interactive chief executive Strauss Zelnick has quietly told you not to expect the full meal, calling the whole thing "one of the hors d'oeuvres," with "appetizers, main course and dessert to follow." So, basically, what we're saying is that the upcoming GTA 6 footage probably isn't going to give you what you're expecting.

What the GTA 6 Extended Look Won't Show on August 27
What it likely won't show

Why Rockstar holds it back

The full map

Scale is a launch-day gut-punch, and a full layout hands dataminers everything early

The GTA 6 Online format and timing

Online arrives weeks after launch, and its monetization is too sensitive to headline now

Any PC release plans

PC always comes later for a second sales wave, and this is a console campaign

Exact unlock times and preload details

Logistics drip out closer to launch, as their own free news cycle

Late-game story and spoilers

Rockstar sells tone and characters in trailers, never the plot

These are informed predictions based on how Rockstar rolled out its last two games.

Starting with the map, Rockstar has never handed over the full shape of a GTA 6 world before the game is out. It teases regions and vibes, it lets you clock a beach here and a swamp there, but the actual scale and layout stays hidden until the moment you are standing on top of it, which works because the sheer size of Los Santos , Liberty City , and Vice City , among others, are one of the franchise's biggest selling points.

They're supposed to knock you flat once you realize how far Leonida sprawls and that gut-punch just won't land right if they showed everything off. Besides, when you hand over a complete map, you also hand dataminers and rival studios the entire blueprint months early. Sure, we can expect to see more corners of the world on the August 27, just do not expect the whole thing laid out.

The second big one is Grand Theft Auto Online . GTA Online arrived about two weeks after Grand Theft Auto V , and Red Dead Online limped out as a beta a month after Red Dead Redemption 2 . Jason Schreier has also confirmed that GTA Online isn't a priority for now . The main focus is the single-player campaign.

Then there is the PC question. GTA 6 is a console game at launch, full stop, with no PC date anywhere in sight. Rockstar has a long, deliberate habit of holding the PC version back for further optimization and a second wave of sales. Announcing a PC release now would undercut such plans. Don't expect any such news until after the game is out.

Another thing is not to count on are the exact unlock details either, the precise launch time, the preload window , the file size, all the stuff you actually need to plan your release day around. Rockstar is not going to waste this by burying it inside a trailer. A cinematic showcase this far out is simply not the venue for a preload schedule.

Finally, do not expect much of the actual story. Rockstar trailers sell a mood and a couple of faces, not the plot. You will almost certainly get more of Jason and Lucia and the Bonnie-and-Clyde energy between them, but you will not get where their story actually goes.

None of this is meant to be a downer . There is plenty the Extended Look almost certainly will show, enough to send the hype meter straight back into the red and then some. You will get a proper look at Jason and Lucia as characters, more of their relationship, more of their voices, more of the tone Rockstar is chasing, you will probably get a real jump in presentation over the trailers, and most definitely, you will get another reminder that November 19 is really when the game is coming out.

The thing everyone is holding their breath for is real gameplay. The actual moment-to-moment business of controlling the two protagonists is where Rockstar will disappoint you. Zelnick has said the presentation will feel more like watching a Netflix show , which is not the same thing as a hands-on-the-controller gameplay breakdown, and that's the whole tell.

Calling your biggest reveal in over a year a mere starter pre-writes both the hype and the excuse in the same sentence. If the Extended Look floors everyone, well, imagine the main course. If it leaves people cold, it was only ever a nibble.

So take the show, Grand Theft Auto VI: An Extended Look , for exactly what it is when it premieres on Netflix on August 27, with the free version landing on other channels six hours later. Why Does GTA 6 Look Different in the New PS5 Commercial?

By Ray Ampoloquio · Aug 18, 2026
Updated Aug 18, 2026

Sony's PS5 ad has no new GTA 6 footage, it just reuses Trailer 2 clips with brighter lighting, full 16:9 framing, and added sound effects.

Sony dropped a new Grand Theft Auto VI clip into the wild on August 17 and within hours Grand Theft Auto fans were doing what they do best: freezing it frame by frame and arguing about it. The truth, as always, isn't quite what fans are making it it out to be. If you rewatched the existing trailers as many times as us, you'll probably feel like something is different - but is any of the footage new?

GTA 6 only shows up three times in a one-minute commercial posted by PlayStation, which is a glossy montage of live-action shots and game footage built to sell PlayStation 5 consoles. You'll see it roughly around the 24, 44, and 52-second marks of the "It Happens on PS5" commercial embedded below, sandwiched between clips of Marvel's Wolverine and God of War Laufey .

As for the question on everyone's minds, no, there is no new footage. Every GTA 6 shot in the ad is lifted straight from the second trailer that dropped back in May 2025. Nobody at Rockstar Games filmed anything new for a console ad. However, it does look a little bit different, probably because Sony's marketing team got their hands on it.

Nearly all of the changes on the newest GTA 6 footage are about presentation. None of it confirms a change to the actual game. Trailer 2 was framed in a wide, cinematic ratio with letterbox bars along the top and bottom, giving it a movie-screen look. The ad strips those off and fills the whole screen in standard 16:9, so you are seeing a bit more of each shot.

The getaway scene, where Jason hangs off the back of a convertible while Lucia drives, also looks brighter, and Lucia's eyebrows are softer and her hair a shade browner. Finally, fresh sound effects got layered in too, including a crisp trunk slam near the end that was not there before. We have, in a sense, got a remaster of GTA 6 footage before GTA 6 .

Almost every single one of the changes between the GTA 6 Trailer 2 footage and the one used on the PS5 ad are merely cosmetic.

From the outside, the latest PS5 ad looks identical from the GTA 6 Trailer 2 footage. A downgrade didn't, or at least, hasn't happened yet, nor did Rockstar redo anyone's faces. Most GTA fans are just theorising or making much ado about anything, like what happened when a "leaked" Netflix listing turned out to be a two-minute fake . The information vacuum intentionally created by Rockstar turns everyone into a forensic analyst.

With that said, this ad is a quiet reminder that GTA 6 has become a machine for selling PlayStations. Back in May, Take-Two Interactive chief executive Strauss Zelnick confirmed Rockstar had signed an exclusive marketing partnership with Sony for the game, and this is what that looks like in practice. The most anticipated title on the planet is now the centerpiece of Sony's flagship hardware campaign , which is also why pre-order links once prominently pointed at PlayStation and quietly stepped around Xbox.

Yet, while Sony has the exclusive deal, the marketing budget, and the prime-time slot, it still had nothing newer to show than the same year-old convertible clip the rest of us have watched a hundred times. Even PlayStation is stuck recycling Trailer 2, because Rockstar is not handing anyone fresh footage until it decides to. The live-action bits, the Miami-flavored shots fans tied to Vice City and a clip staged on a billboard in Warsaw, are Sony dressing up old material to feel like an event.

The good news here is that the the actual new look is only days away. Rockstar's Extended Look hits Netflix on August 27 , and with GTA 6 now under 100 days from its November 19 launch , we'll know if any real changes will show up soon enough.

GTA 6 gameplay allegedly leaks ahead of planned Netflix reveal
Videos claiming to show Grand Theft Auto 6 are being circulated online

Video Game News
18th Aug 2026 / 7:30 pm

Posted by Andy Robinson

Videos claiming to show Grand Theft Auto 6 gameplay are being circulated online by a group protesting its lack of a physical disc version.
The footage, which VGC is not able to share but is being widely circulated on social media, appears to show gameplay of the much-anticipated Rockstar sequel, a week before its planned Netflix reveal.

One video shows Jason, one of GTA 6’s two protagonists, playing a basketball mini-game at the house featured in the game’s reveal trailer. Notably, the footage shows Jason increasing a ‘focus’ stat for successfully landing a shot, suggesting the game could feature RPG-style mechanics.
A second video alleging to show GTA 6 gameplay features a driving scene, in which Jason crashes into a delivery vehicle before engaging in a fist fight. If authentic, the footage appears to confirm that vehicles will require gas to drive.
Cyberleek, the group claiming responsibility for the alleged videos, said it had targeted Rockstar parent Take-Two in protest of its decision to sell digital pre-orders for GTA 6 and not offer a physical version . The group also published what it claims to be the game map for GTA 6.

At the time of publication, there is suggestion that some of the alleged GTA 6 videos have been pulled down following copyright strikes. VGC has asked Rockstar for comment.
If authentic, the media will represent at least the third time GTA 6 has been shown ahead of a planned reveal via leaked footage. In September 2022, one of the games industry’s most high-profile data leaks saw over an hour of GTA 6 development footage published online .
Then, in December 2023, the game’s debut trailer leaked online ahead of a planned official release.

An extended look at GTA 6 is premiering on Netflix later this month. Grand Theft Auto VI: An Extended Look premieres on Netflix on August 27, at 12pm PT / 3pm ET / 8pm BST. It will also launch on the Rockstar Games YouTube channel and the GTA 6 website six hours later.
Neither Rockstar nor Netflix has shared more information on the presentation or how long it will last.
“See an extended look at Grand Theft Auto 6 , the next evolution in the groundbreaking Grand Theft Auto series,” Netflix’s official description reads.

“Grand Theft Auto reveals have become cultural moments in their own right,” Netflix VP of nonfiction series Brandon Riegg said in a statement.
“The anticipation and fandom around Grand Theft Auto VI is unprecedented, and we’re honored that Rockstar Games has partnered with us to debut the next part of the Grand Theft Auto story with Netflix members first.
“It’s a reflection of what we hope Netflix is becoming – a place where the most ambitious storytelling, from any medium, can find the biggest possible audience.”

GTA 6 Leaker Threatens Rockstar And Other Major Publishers With Further Action

The newest set of GTA 6 leaks has rocked the gaming world. It remains to be seen what Rockstar Games’ reaction to this is going to be, but we do know that the leaker, who has outed themselves, may not be done with leaked footage and information about GTA 6 and other major games.

Several years on from the infamous Rockstar breach that saw an astronomical amount of GTA 6 content become public knowledge, something similar happened on August 18, when new GTA 6 leaks flooded the internet .

Only this time, the individual/group not only became known almost immediately, but it has also sent out an ominous warning to all publishers.

More ‘Disruptions’ Planned Until Rockstar Apologizes & Undoes ‘Harm’

Credit to Rockstar Games

An alleged video of Jason playing basketball in GTA 6 appeared on social media, and all hell broke loose once the realization sank in that it might be real.

New videos and leaks emerged soon after, including reports of a GTA 6 honor system and the full map leaking.

More Insider Gaming: Star Citizen Live Stream Goes Wrong as Devs Look Uncomfortable Playing It

Social media identified ‘CYBERLEEK’ as the culprit, and we think it’s just one person, although this has yet to be confirmed.

A full statement from CYBERLEEK goes through their three commandments, which will bring gaming publishers into the spotlight over three things:

Commandment I: Thou shalt not sell digital preorders.

Commandment II: Thou shalt not sell fake single-player DLC.

Commandment III: Thou shalt preserve single-player content.

The MO is to punish publishers who have created “one monetization scheme at a time” and to stop these practices, which have become the norm in gaming.

Here is the edict:

“CYBERLEEK has been patient. That patience is over. What follows are three commandments. If CYBERLEEK targets a publisher, it is because that publisher broke one. CYBERLEEK will not stop until they issue a public statement and apology with a concrete commitment to be better. Words are not enough; restitution is mandatory.”

So, Rockstar Games needs to apologize for locking content behind the Ultimate Edition, for example, and general GTA 6 digital pre-orders.

More Insider Gaming: XBOX’s Surprise Sequel Could Be A Recent Franchise

However, the ‘Final Word’ makes it clear that it’s not just Rockstar being attacked, or in danger of being attacked:

“These three commandments are the floor—not the ceiling—of what is acceptable. If publishers violete them, they will be targeted. CYBERLEEK will continue to disrupt their operations until they issue a public apology with a concrete committment to fix the harm they caused. No proovate negotiations. No quiet settlements. The public sees it, or the “leeks” do not stop. Publishers should beware. If CYBERLEEK can reach Rockstar, no one is safe. This is a message to all big corpo: behave, or be the next target.

This is the CYBERLEEK edict, and it is non-negotiable.”

You can read the full thing for yourself below.

— Cameron (@salbertMVP) August 18, 2026

How much more footage or leaks does CYBERLEEK have on GTA 6?

Which other games could potentially be targeted by CYBERLEEK? If there were anything to possibly disrupt the almost inevitable release of Grand Theft Auto 6, we could be witnessing it.

How far do you think Cyberleek is willing to go? Let us know on the Insider Gaming Discord server .

Alleged GTA 6 Gameplay Footage Leaks Online

It has been claimed that a major data breach has occurred linked to Grand Theft Auto 6 that has resulted in gameplay for the upcoming open-world epic leaking online. In recent hours, several clips have surfaced on social media, all of which are being hit with DMCA strikes by Take-Two Interactive, which almost always lends credence to the content.

In-development footage of the game and claimed features have also appeared online, across social circles and gaming forums worldwide. Insider Gaming understands that preview events for GTA 6 are underway, but it’s not clear if the alleged leak footage originates from the event.

Given the quality of some of the footage, it’s unlikely.

GTA 6 Leaks Seem to Appear on Social Media

In a series of clips that have surfaced online, seemingly tied to another batch of GTA 6 leaks, several elements of the upcoming Rockstar Games title have been ‘revealed’. This includes exploration aspects, a hefty six-star wanted level, some side activities, a new, never-before-seen location, and an interaction between NPCs.

There are also examples of loadout systems, refuelling mechanics for cars, some of the in-game gadgets like the phone system, and a look at how stamina works.

Again, it’s worth stressing in no uncertain terms that these leaks are not corroborated or certified in any way, aside from the fact that Take-Two is actively striking down any examples that appear online.

That’s why I’ve not replicated them here, of course.

RELATED: Paying $100 For GTA 6 Makes Sense

Most of the leaks reference a bizarre cryptocurrency link that should be ignored at all costs. It says that, if you want more footage, head to this weird site , but I cannot say strongly enough that you should not do that .

The first ‘leak’ surfaced a few hours ago, at the time of writing, and showcased Jason playing basketball outside his beachfront house. It was a bit janky, and many believed it to be an AI construct before the DMCA strikes started flying in.

It has been reported by some that the leaker obtained and revealed the footage as a way of protesting the digital-only release of GTA 6, slated to occur on November 19th.

RELATED: Will GTA 6 Be Delayed Again?

For now, the only official reveal or dose of gameplay on the horizon is tied to the Netflix ‘extended look’ that’s being released on August 27.
